{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "Marisol had learned the house by its sounds before she ever learned it by its rooms. The kettle that ticked as it cooled. The third stair, which spoke only when someone tried to be quiet on it. The radiator in the front room that knocked twice at six each morning, as if asking permission to begin.

So when the knocking came at four, she was awake before she understood why.

She lay still and listened. Two knocks, a pause, two more. Not the radiator. The rhythm was wrong, too deliberate, and it came from below her, from the cellar she had not opened since the agent handed her the keys and said, a little too lightly, that the previous owner had kept wine down there.

She found her robe by touch. The hall was blue with the hour, the windows more felt than seen. At the top of the cellar stairs she stood with her hand on the switch and did not press it.

The knocking stopped.

It was the silence after that decided her. A silence with attention in it. She pressed the switch, and the bulb below came on reluctant and yellow, and she went down.

The cellar was smaller than the house had promised. Shelves along one wall, empty. A drain in the floor. And against the far wall, a door she had not been told about, painted the same grey as the stone around it, with a brass handle worn bright at the center.

As she watched, the handle turned a quarter inch, and settled back.

"Hello," said Marisol, because it seemed rude not to."}
